title: Vilsonovo šetalište
description: A pockmarked four-storey apartment block on the Miljacka embankment, photographed from a footbridge beside the Vrbanja bridge: a south-east-facing stucco facade with balconies and tiled dormers, and the high-rise of the Parliament complex rising behind.

attribution.title: File:Vilsonovo Šetalište.jpg
attribution.creator: Fanny Schertzer
transformations: all EXIF/XMP metadata stripped (incl. the EXIF GPS position and the embedded sRGB ICC profile; the pixels are sRGB, so colours are unchanged)

notes: Position and heading: Commons {{Location|43|51|11.8|N|18|24|23.24|E|heading:NNW}}, which the Commons API lists as the camera location (43.85327778, 18.40645556); it lies on the footbridge over the Miljacka (OSM way/483747123, bridge=yes) whose railing is in the foreground. 'NNW' is a 16-point compass direction (±11.25°), taken as 337.5°.

The original JPEG also carries EXIF GPS 43°51.2183'N 18°24.4261'E (43.853638, 18.407102), about 66 m north-east of the Commons position, and is not used: through the app's loader (pitch solving + auto-alignment) a camera there with the same NNW heading puts none of the 46 windows on the photographed block (9 placed in all, rows 68 cm out of line after alignment), whereas from the Commons position 40 are placed and auto-alignment finds the rows already level within 9 cm and leaves the camera unchanged. A user uploading the original file would start from the EXIF position.
hfov 40.3° from EXIF 35 mm-equivalent focal length 49 mm (FocalLength 33 mm on the APS-C Sony NEX-7) on a 3:2 landscape frame (diagonal convention: horizontal side = 43.27 mm × 3/√13 = 36.0 mm).

Pitch 8° estimated by eye: the head of the pedestrian on the far pavement (≈ 1.6–1.7 m) is at ≈ row 1040 of 1333, ≈ 374 px below the image centre; with f = 1000 / tan(20.15°) ≈ 2725 px that is atan(374 / 2725) ≈ 7.8°.
Lens height 1.6 m above the street (assumed); the footbridge deck is treated as street level.
hfovRange = [0.5, 1.05] × the EXIF-derived hfov: a crop can only narrow the field of view and nothing widens it, so auto-alignment keeps the FOV inside these bounds.
